study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Ge et al., Lancet Digit Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study aims to identify the optimal approach for normative modeling of brain morphometry by benchmarking algorithms and optimizing parameters.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We aimed to identify the optimal approach for normative modelling of brain morphometric data through systematic empirical benchmarking, by quantifying the accuracy of di/uniFB00erent algorithms and identifying parameters that optimised model performance.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study collated data from 87 datasets with specific inclusion criteria (no psychiatric/medical morbidity, cognitive impairment). Sample size (37,407) and exclusion (extreme values) are described.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: We collated de-identified data from 87 datasets... selected to include highquality neuroimaging measures... from participants who did not have psychiatric, medical, and neurological morbidity and cognitive impairment... A total of 37 407 healthy individuals... included.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Sex-specific models were developed. Age and global neuroimaging measures were used as covariates. Site effects were addressed by ComBat-GAM or random effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Sex-specific normative models were developed... Model optimisation involved the evaluation of improvements... by adding... global neuroimaging measures... scanner vendor type... The potential e/uniFB00ect of site... was addressed both by handling site as a random factor and by site-harmonisation using ComBat-GAM...

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: 87 datasets are used and listed in the appendix (Table S1).
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: We collated de-identified data from 87 datasets from Europe, Australia, the USA, South Africa, and east Asia (appendix 1 p 2; appendix 2).

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The study uses secondary data from 87 existing datasets. Acquisition protocols varied.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Acquisition protocols and scanner vendors varied across datasets (appendix 2).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing using FreeSurfer standard pipelines is described. Quality control procedures (ENIGMA pipeline, Qoala-T, Euler number) are detailed.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: Morphometric feature extraction from whole-brain T 1 -weighted images was implemented with the standard pipelines in the FreeSurfer image analysis suite... For samples participating in the ENIGMA Lifespan Working Group... quality assessment followed the ENIGMA consortium pipeline...

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study used a stratified 80/20 split for training/testing and 5-fold cross-validation within the training set.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Sex-specific subsamples... split into a training subset (80%) and a test subset (20%)... The models were trained with five-fold cross-validation (5F-CV) in the corresponding sex-specific training subset...

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The models were applied to independent datasets (SLIM and QTAB for longitudinal stability, HCP-EP for clinical relevance) not used in model development.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The Southwest Longitudinal Imaging Multimodal Study (SLIM) and the Queensland Twin Adolescent Brain Study (QTAB) were used to test the longitudinal stability... There is no participant overlap... HCP-EP cohort... used to test... relevance...

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: Eight algorithms were benchmarked, including MFPR, GAMLSS, GPR, etc. MFPR was selected as optimal. Key settings (polynomials, etc.) are described.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: The data for each morphometric measure were analysed with the following algorithms: (1) ordinary least squares regression... (8) multivariate fractional polynomial regression (MFPR)... optimised with non-linear polynomials for age...

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Performance was assessed using MAE, RMSE, and explained variance.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The mean absolute error (MAE)... supplemented by the root mean square error (RMSE)... and by explained variance.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: The split ratio (80/20) is reported. Stratification by site and age was performed. Age distributions are shown in supplementary figures. Sample sizes for datasets are in Table S1.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: Sex-specific subsamples... split into a training subset (80%) and a test subset (20%), through stratified randomisation by scanning site and age.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Code and models are available via CentileBrain. Software versions (FreeSurfer, R packages) are specified.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: The model and scripts described here are freely available through CentileBrain... https://centilebrain.org... FreeSurfer version 7.1.0... scikit-learn package (version 1.2.2)...

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: The HCP-EP cohort selection is described, citing the original publication. Diagnostic groups (early psychosis) and sample size (91 patients, 57 healthy) are reported.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: The HCP-EP cohort comprises 91 individuals with early psychosis and 57 healthy individuals... For diagnostic status... see... Demro C, et al. The psychosis human connectome project: an overview.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: The study predicted symptom severity from Z-scores but did not explicitly mention controlling for clinical covariates (medication, etc.) in the deviation analysis or prediction models beyond basic demographics implicitly handled by the normative model.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: We did not include an exhaustive list of potential explanatory variables... regional Z-scores... were entered into separate ridge regression models... to predict the psychosis score...

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The Human Connectome Project-Early Psychosis Study (HCP-EP) is the data source.

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample size (91 patients, 57 controls), sex (48F/100M total), and age range (16-35) are reported. Diagnosis is Early Psychosis.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: 91 individuals with early psychosis and 57 healthy individuals (total sample 48 females and 100 males; age range 16·67-35·67 years).

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: The Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) was used.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: Psychosis score of the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Z-scores were used to predict diagnosis and symptoms. The study discusses the advantage of Z-scores over observed measures.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: Normative deviation score for each region was defined as... Z-scores... We tested whether normative brain regional Z-scores have an advantage... in predicting diagnostic status...
